title: Why a local variable can't be state

slides.say: Here is a gallery with a Next button. Clicking it does nothing. Why?
The click handler updates a local variable called index. But the screen never changes.

slides.text: 1. Local variables don’t survive renders: each render starts from scratch.
slides.say: Problem one. Local variables do not persist. When React renders again, it starts from scratch, so index is zero again.

slides.text: 2. Changing a local variable doesn’t trigger a render.
slides.say: Problem two. Changing a local variable does not tell React to render again. It has no idea anything changed.

slides.text: You need to retain data AND trigger a render. That is what state does.
slides.say: So you need two things: keep the data between renders, and trigger a new render. That is exactly what state gives you.
